quote: Well, yeah, looking at your address here, I mean, your roof looks really good for solar, a lot of sun there. Just south facing roof as well.
stewart_read: The rep asserts a favorable satellite read on the roof before actually confirming what he's looking at — the customer later corrects him at 05:15 ('You're probably looking at the garage'), revealing the rep was describing the wrong structure the whole time.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive filler to sound diligent rather than a genuine misread — but the correction at 05:15 confirms it was a real error, not just imprecise phrasing.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to verify satellite orientation against customer-confirmed structure identity before stating roof quality as fact — a wrong assertion here undermines credibility on a detail-oriented customer.

quote: I think it's, like, 400 a month.
stewart_read: The rep did attempt a partial reframe immediately after capture ('We'll definitely see if we could, you know, cut that back at least, save you some money'), but it stayed generic and never tied the $400 figure to a specific savings-against-utility frame or reinforced it later in the call.
alternative_hypothesis: Full flip executed — rejected because the rep's line stays vague ('at least,' 'you know') rather than turning the $400 into a concrete reason to act now.
coaching_implication: Credit the rep for reacting to the number immediately, but coach him to make the flip specific and repeat it near the close ('that $400 a month is what we're going after') rather than letting it fade after one soft line.

quote: It's in trust. It's my brother's trust and I'm a trustee.
stewart_read: This is fiduciary/title complexity, not a co-decision-maker-on-title scenario the spouse_decision protocol governs — the schema has no precise anchor for trustee-held property, so this is a genuine schema gap rather than a missed protocol application.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be mapped to protocols.spouse_decision as a co-owner analog, but rejected because that protocol is about who attends the appointment for a joint decision, not about who holds legal signing authority over a trust asset.
coaching_implication: Flag for Kenny: does Ion have a defined path for trust-held/rental properties where the trustee, not a resident owner, is the decision-maker? The rep handled it by simply proceeding, which may or may not be correct procedure.

quote: I probably have enough electric capacity to push it back up to the house because everything runs through the house.
stewart_read: Customer discloses he has a generator and details his home's electrical routing capacity — a technical engagement signal and a potential battery/backup interest that the rep doesn't probe or flag.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to notice generator/backup-power comments as a Powerwall conversation opener — even a single question ('are you looking for battery backup too?') would surface intent for the closer to build on.

quote: Do you have a program where you put a roof on too?
stewart_read: The customer asks directly about roofing, and the rep already has the roof-age data in hand (house ~20 years, garage ~5 years, captured at 05:36-05:40) — the miss isn't failing to ask about the roof, it's failing to route that already-known data to the roofing team in real time.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as appropriate scope discipline (deferring to specialist) — rejected because the schema's cross_sell_signals.roof_replacement_planned explicitly calls for the setter to bridge and co-route in the moment, not just mention that a specialist exists.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to actively flag the older 20-year house roof to the roofing team when the customer raises it, rather than giving a generic 'I don't know a ton of details' deflection — the data is already there to route.

quote: I don't know, like, a ton of the details, especially for the roofs, but our, our specialist would know know all about that for you.
stewart_read: The rep correctly avoids fabricating roofing program details, but the admission ('I don't know a ton') combined with no concrete routing action leaves the roofing interest unanchored — a clean escape-hatch line would have been sharper.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as good scope discipline since he doesn't overexplain — accepted as partially correct, but the lack of a routing commitment is still a gap.
coaching_implication: Replace the vague knowledge admission with the universal escape hatch plus an explicit routing promise, e.g., flagging the file for the roofing team given the 20-year-old house roof already on record.
